title: Written promises and proposed substitutes
summary: The notes preserve historical disagreement over whether form or commercial context should replace consideration.
notes: Pillans & Rose’s discussion of writing is set against Rann v. Hughes. The Uniform Written Obligations Act’s limited enactment and statutory presumptions illustrate the difference between writing as proof and writing as an enforcement basis. Farber and Matheson’s reform proposal, Hillman’s empirical response, and other commentary ask how doctrine works and might change. A proposal is not encoded as an enacted rule.
